intro.title: useLayoutEffect vs useEffect
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that demonstrates the difference between `useLayoutEffect` and `useEffect`. You will learn how these hooks handle side effects and when to use each one based on their timing in the component lifecycle. The core concept involves understanding synchronous vs. asynchronous DOM updates and how they impact visual rendering. You will use Vue's Composition API with `onMounted` and `onUpdated` to simulate React-like effect behavior, focusing on JavaScript timing and DOM manipulation. By the end, you'll know how to choose the right effect for tasks like measurements or animations to avoid layout thrashing.
intro.usecase: In real Vue applications, understanding the timing difference between onMounted (similar to useEffect) and onUpdated (similar to useLayoutEffect) is crucial for smooth UI interactions. When building dynamic dashboards with charts that need immediate measurement after DOM updates, onUpdated ensures calculations happen before the browser paints, preventing visual flicker. This pattern is essential for form validation that requires checking input dimensions, responsive navigation menus that adjust based toggled content, or modal positioning that depends on sibling element sizes. Developers use these hooks to coordinate DOM-dependent operations with the browser's rendering cycle, creating polished user experiences without layout thrashing.
